¹⁶ The priests went into the inner chambers of the LORD's temple to purify it, carrying out everything unclean they found and bringing it to the courtyard of the LORD's house, where the Levites took it and hauled it out to the Kidron Valley. ¹⁷ They began the purification on the first day of the first month, and by the eighth day they had reached the LORD's porch; over the next eight days they sanctified the house of the LORD, and by the sixteenth day of the first month the work was finished. ¹⁸ Then they came in to King Hezekiah and reported, "We have cleansed the entire house of the LORD—the altar of burnt offering with all its equipment, and the table of the showbread with all its vessels. ¹⁹ Every piece that King Ahaz threw aside during his reign of unfaithfulness, we have prepared and consecrated. ²¹ They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. Necho took Jehoahaz his brother and carried him off to Egypt. ⁵ Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.

⁶ Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against him, bound him in chains, and took him to Babylon. ⁷ Nebuchadnezzar also took some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and placed them in his temple there. ⁸ The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, the detestable things he did, and what was found against him — all are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. And his son Jehoiachin reigned in his place. ⁹ Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did evil in the eyes of the LORD. ¹⁰ In the spring, King Nebuchadnezzar sent for him and brought him to Babylon, along with the most precious articles from the house of the LORD. He made Zedekiah, Jehoiachin's brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.

¹¹ Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. ¹² He did evil in the eyes of the LORD his God and did not humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah, who spoke the word of the LORD. ¹³ He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear an oath in God's name; he became stubborn and hardened his heart against turning to the LORD, the God of Israel. ¹⁴ Furthermore, all the leaders of the priests and all the people became more and more unfaithful, following the detestable practices of the surrounding nations and defiling the house of the LORD, which he had made holy in Jerusalem. ¹⁵ The LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent word to them again and again through his messengers, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.

¹⁶ But they mocked God's messengers, despised his words, and ridiculed his prophets until the LORD's wrath was aroused against his people and there was no remedy. ¹⁷ So God brought up against them the king of the Babylonians, who killed their young men with the sword in the sanctuary itself, sparing neither young man nor young woman, neither the elderly nor the frail. God handed them all over to Nebuchadnezzar. ¹⁸ All the articles from the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the LORD's house and the treasures of the king and his officials — all of these Nebuchadnezzar brought to Babylon. ¹⁹ They burned God's house, broke down the wall of Jerusalem, burned all its palaces, and destroyed everything of value there. ²⁰ And those who survived the sword were carried off to Babylon, where they became slaves to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the rise of the Persian kingdom.

²¹ This fulfilled the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah: the land finally enjoyed its sabbath rest, lying desolate all the while the sabbath was observed, until the seventy years were complete. ²² In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the LORD moved the heart of Cyrus to fulfill the word he had spoken through Jeremiah. Cyrus issued a proclamation throughout his kingdom, and also put it in writing: ²³ "This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: 'The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has appointed me to build a temple for him at Jerusalem in Judah. Any of his people among you — may the LORD your God be with you. Let them go up.'"
